title: SmartIO: A Lightweight End-to-End Workflow for Runtime I/O Optimization of HPC Systems
problem: I/O subsystem is a critical bottleneck in HPC systems. Existing optimization approaches require offline tuning, exhaustive parameter searches, or extensive ML model training - all time-consuming and resource-intensive.
motivation: Modern HPC systems have complex I/O hierarchies (storage, cache, network). Automated optimization at runtime without prior training/profiling would enable adaptive performance. Need lightweight runtime solution.
method: SmartIO uses context-free grammars to predict future I/O calls during runtime, learns I/O characteristics from predictions, applies rules-based mapping engine constructed from literature review and empirical evaluation to optimize I/O operations proactively.
key_novelty: Runtime prediction of I/O patterns using context-free grammars; rules-based optimization engine bypassing need for ML model training; negligible runtime overhead.
contributions: Context-free grammar-based I/O call prediction at runtime
Rules-based mapping engine for translating insights into optimizations
Lightweight end-to-end workflow avoiding expensive training/profiling
Significant speedups on real HPC benchmarks (IOR and Flash-X)
limitations: Abstract only; unclear how CFG captures diverse I/O patterns; rules construction methodology not detailed; applicability to emerging workloads (streaming, ML I/O) unclear.
